newsitem.title: JAPAN: Clarke says Rubin still sees strong dlr desirable.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says Rubin still sees strong dlr desirable.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke told a news conference in Tokyo on Friday that U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin continued to believe that a strong dollar was desirable.
Asked about the likely phrasing in any Group of Seven communique after next month's G7 finance ministers' meeting, he said:
"Recently the G7 has welcomed the strength of the dollar and I have welcomed the strength of the dollar...I know Bob Rubin continues to believe a strong dollar is desirable."

Clarke, who arrived on Wednesday for talks with Japanese officials and business executives, reiterated Britain's stance that it would decide on whether to participate in the European Monetary Union at a "sensible time".
But he added that if Britain did stay out, "I don't think the City of London will be disadvantaged as the major financial centre of Europe."
